# homarr_board (Resource)

Manages a Homarr board — a dashboard page.

A new board is created exactly as the Homarr UI creates one: with one empty section and two layouts, a 3-column *Mobile* layout and a *Base* layout with `column_count` columns. To start from a board designed in the UI instead, use `homarr_board_copy`.

The widgets and app tiles placed *on* a board are not manageable here. Homarr's REST API can add a tile (`POST /api/boards/items`, see the `homarr_board_add_item` action), move or resize one, and rewrite a whole board (`PUT /api/boards/{id}/content`), but nothing over REST reads tiles, sections or layouts back, so they cannot be reconciled declaratively.

Renaming, changing `is_public` and destroying a board need *full* access to it: being its creator, a `full` user or group grant, or the `board-full-all` permission, which admins have. Homarr answers anyone else with 404, which the provider reports as an access error while the board is still listed.

~> **Note** Homarr makes a new board its creator's desktop home board whenever that user has none selected — not only the first board, and again after `is_home = false` cleared the slot — so `is_home` can come back `true` on a board that never asked for it. Declaring `is_home = false` clears that again right after creation. `is_home` and `is_mobile_home` are the home boards *of the user behind the API key*; the instance-wide defaults live in `homarr_server_board_settings`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "homarr_board" "infra" {
  name         = "infra"
  column_count = 12
  is_public    = false
}

# Board names double as URL slugs, so only letters, digits, hyphens and
# underscores are accepted — "infra core" would be rejected by Homarr. Names are
# unique regardless of case, so "Infra" next to "infra" is refused before the
# board is created; the plan already warns about it.
resource "homarr_board" "public_status" {
  name         = "status-page"
  column_count = 6
  is_public    = true
}

# is_home and is_mobile_home select the home board of the user behind the API
# key. Setting one to false clears that slot again (Homarr 2.3.0 or newer); to
# move the flag, set it on another board instead.
resource "homarr_board" "landing" {
  name           = "landing"
  column_count   = 10
  is_public      = true
  is_home        = true
  is_mobile_home = true
}

# The base layout id is returned only when a board is created. The
# homarr_board_add_item action takes it as layout_id to put a tile at a given
# position on the desktop layout.
output "landing_base_layout_id" {
  value = homarr_board.landing.base_layout_id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `column_count` (Number) Number of columns in the board's base layout, between 1 and 24. The mobile layout always starts with 3.

~> **Note** The column count lives on the board's layouts, and no REST call reads layouts back. Writing them (`PUT /api/boards/{id}/layouts`, Homarr 2.3.0) needs the complete layout list including the mobile layout's id, which no REST response contains. Changing this value therefore forces a new board, and the provider cannot detect a column count changed through the Homarr UI.
- `name` (String) Board name, also used in the board's URL. Only ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_` are allowed; spaces and other punctuation are rejected by Homarr.

Names must be unique, compared case-insensitively. Homarr's REST create does not check that itself — an exact duplicate fails with an internal error, and one differing only in case is accepted although the board's URL then reaches only one of the two — so the provider checks the name against the boards the API key can see. It refuses a name differing only in case right before creating the board. While planning it only warns, because a plan cannot see another board being renamed or destroyed earlier in the same apply, nor tell a tainted board being replaced from a clash.

### Optional

- `is_home` (Boolean) Whether this board is the desktop home board of the user behind the API key. Leave it out to report whatever Homarr has.

The home board is a per-user singleton, so selecting one board deselects whichever board held the flag before. Declaring `is_home = true` on two boards makes them fight over it on every apply. The board that loses the flag is not re-read during that apply, so its state reports `true` until the next refresh.

~> **Setting this to `false` requires Homarr 2.3.0 or newer.** Clearing a home board goes through `PATCH /api/users/preferences`, which arrived in 2.3.0 and is the first endpoint that can address the API key's own user without knowing its id; older releases can clear a home board only through `PATCH /api/users/changeHome` with an explicit user id, which no REST call reveals for the key's own user. Homarr also refuses to make a board private while it is an *instance-wide* home board set through `homarr_server_board_settings`.
- `is_mobile_home` (Boolean) Whether this board is the mobile home board of the user behind the API key. Behaves exactly like `is_home`, against Homarr's separate mobile slot. Unlike `is_home` it is never assigned automatically.
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether the board is visible without authentication. Defaults to `false`. Homarr refuses to make a board private while it is an *instance-wide* home board — `home_board_id` or `mobile_home_board_id` in `homarr_server_board_settings`, not the per-user `is_home`.

### Read-Only

- `base_layout_id` (String) Identifier of the board's base layout — the desktop one — as Homarr returned it when the provider created the board. It is the only layout id any REST response contains. Pass it as `layout_id` to the `homarr_board_add_item` action to put a new tile at a given position; other tools can use it with `PATCH /api/boards/{boardId}/items/{itemId}/layouts/{layoutId}` to move or resize a tile.

No REST call reads layouts back, so this is known only for boards created by provider 0.3.0 or newer. It is null after an import and for boards created earlier.
- `creator_id` (String) Identifier of the user that created the board. That is the user behind the API key only for boards that key created; an imported board keeps its original creator, and the creator always has full access to the board.
- `id` (String) Homarr-generated identifier of the board.
- `logo_image_url` (String) Board logo URL, as reported by Homarr. Set this through `homarr_board_settings`, which owns the board's appearance.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Boards are imported as "<board_id>,<column_count>". The column count has to be
# supplied by hand because Homarr's REST API does not report it; read it from the
# board's layout settings in the UI (the UI default is 10).
#
# Importing with a bare id is rejected on purpose: column_count would land in
# state as null, and because a change to it forces replacement, the next plan
# would propose destroying the board you just imported.
terraform import homarr_board.infra csgjeb9j3y2mflvznts1ip0w,12

# The board can also be named instead of identified, as "name=<name>,<column_count>".
# The name is matched exactly first, then case-insensitively.
terraform import homarr_board.infra name=infra,12

# base_layout_id stays null after an import: Homarr returns a board's layout id
# only in the response that created it.
```
